title: Positioning: static, relative, absolute, fixed and sticky

videos.script: Until now, every box in this course went where the page put it. One after another, top to bottom, each pushing the next one down. {{flow}} That is called the normal flow, and it is right for almost everything. Text reads in order, and a longer paragraph makes room for itself. {{badge}} Some things do not belong in the flow. A small label in the corner of a card. A button to chat that stays on the screen while you scroll. A heading that sticks to the top until its section has passed. A notice laid over the whole page. {{position}} The position property is how CSS takes a box out of the flow, or half out of it. Relative, absolute, fixed and sticky. Each one answers two questions differently. Does the box still take up space? And what are its top and left measured from? {{escape}} You will watch a label measured against the wrong box and fly to the corner of the page. And you will watch a menu with a z-index of nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine sit underneath a box with a z-index of two. {{end}} Both have a rule behind them, and once you know the rule, neither is a mystery. {{close}}
